Hon'ble Shri Justice Ravindra Kumar Agrawal Judgment on Board 15.02.2024 1.

This appeal under Section 173 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 has been filed by the non-applicant No.3, the Insurance Company, challenging the award passed by the 2nd Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Dantewada, District - South Bastar, Chhattisgarh, in Claim Case No. 24/2017, by which the claim application of present respondent Nos. 1 to 5 was partly allowed and an amount of Rs.70,83,105/- has been awarded in favour of the claimants.

sentences.text: 2. Brief facts of the case are that on 24.09.2016, when the deceased Shailendra Pratap Singh was going to Police Line, Karli from his house, when he reached near Karli gate, the offending vehicle Truck bearing its registration number C.G.18 H 1090, which was being rashly and negligently driven by the non-applicant No.1 Madan Manjhi and owned by non-applicant No.2 Manoj Gupta and insured by the non-applicant No.3/appellant The Oriental Insurance Company Limited dashed the deceased by which he received injuries and died on the spot.
The accident was reported to the police and the non-applicant No.1 was prosecuted for the offence under Section 279, 304-A of IPC.

The claimants have filed the claim case before the Claims Tribunal for the total compensation of Rs.1,23,04,712/- on account of death of the deceased on various heads and pleaded that the deceased Shailendra Pratap Singh was Head Constable at 9th Battalion of the Police Department and was earning Rs.36,227/- per month.
The claimants are dependent upon the income of the deceased and thereby they claimed the compensation amount.
The non-applicant No.1 remain ex-party before the Claims Tribunal.

The non-applicant No.2 contested the case of the claimant and submitted written statement and pleaded that the driver of the vehicle is having valid and effective driving license at the time of accident and if, any amount towards compensation is awarded, the liability to pay the same is upon the Insurance Company as the vehicle was duly insured with the Insurance Company.

3. The non-applicant No.3, the Insurance Company has also contested the claim of the claimants by filing their separate written statement and have pleaded that the offending vehicle was being driven in violation of the policy condition on the date of accident.
The Driver was not having valid and effective driving license at the time of accident and therefore the Insurance Company is not liable to pay compensation.

4. On the basis of the pleadings made by parties, the Claims Tribunal has framed 6 issues and after recording of the evidence of the parties and hearing them, passed the award of Rs.70,83,105/- in favour of the claimants on various heads and liability to pay compensation fastened upon the non-applicant No.3, the Insurance Company.
Hence this appeal by the Insurance Company.
5. Learned counsel for the appellant would submit that the amount awarded in favour of the claimant are exorbitant.
The tribunal has not deducted from the monthly income of the deceased towards Naxal Allowance, Ration Allowance and therefore the amount awarded is on higher side.

He would further submit that the deceased himself was negligent in the accident and therefore,

2 considering the contributory negligence on the part of the deceased, the amount of compensation should have been reduced to the extent to the percentage of contributory negligence from the deceased side.

He would further submit that in the criminal case registered against the non-applicant No.1, he has been acquitted from the Court of learned Judicial Magistrate First Class,
Dantewada which proves that the offending vehicle was not involved in the accident, despite that the impugned award has been passed.

He would further submits that the eye witness of the accident the Dives Beer Nag has not been examined by the claimant whereas the said eye witness was examined by the Criminal Court and his evidence has not been considered by the Tribunal and therefore the impugned award is liable to be set aside.

6. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondents No.1 to 5 have supporting the award passed by the learned tribunal and submitted that the claimants have proved their case by examining the eye witness to the accident as AW-4 Sakha Ram Kunjam who has duly prove the accident.

From the evidence of AW-4 Sakha Ram Kunjam, it has duly been proved that the accident occurred only by the rash and negligently driving of the offending vehicle and there is no contributary or composite negligence from the deceased side.

He would further submits that the deceased was posted at 9th Battalion, Karli which was highly naxal affected area and therefore naxal allowances was granted by the department as per rules which cannot be deducted while assessing the compensation amount.

He would further submits that so far as ration allowance is concerned, it cannot be deducted for assessment of the compensation because ration allowance is to be granted at every place of his posting.
It is not that it cannot be granted to the deceased when he would be posted other than the place of 9th Battalion.

So far as the acquittal of the non-applicant No.1 from the criminal case is concerned he submit that the acquittal may be on some other grounds and even if the non-applicant No.1 is acquittal from the criminal case it would not affects the merit of the present claim case because in the claim case the accident has been proved and death of the deceased by the accident has also been proved by the witness as well as the documents and therefore, he prayed for dismissal of the appeal filed by the Insurance Company.
7. I have heard the learned counsel for the parties and consider the rival submission by perusing the material available on record.

8. So far as the argument advanced by learned counsel for the Insurance Company relating to the deductions towards the naxal allowance and ration allowance is concerned, from perusal of the Ex.
A/11, the naxal allowance has not been specifically mentioned, however, the pay slip bears special ration allowance of Rs.2000/-.

The submission of the learned counsel for the appellant is that official witness AW/3, Sanjay Kumar Mandavi has admitted in his cross examination that the naxal allowance and ration allowance could not be payable when the employees are posted outside of the naxal area and therefore, there should be deduction towards naxal allowances and ration allowances.

The submissions of the learned counsel for the appellant is not acceptable because on the date of accident he was posted there and the benefit of naxal allowance and ration allowance were extending to him.

He may continue his services there at naxal area for entire tenure or he may not have remained there for longer time but the fact remains that he was posted on the date of accident in naxal area and the benefit towards the same was extending to him, therefore this Court is of the view that the view taken by the tribunal is correct.

sentences.text: So far as the argument of contributory negligence is concerned the claimants have examined the eye-witness AW-4 Sakharam Kunjam.
He has stated in his deposition that the driver of the offending vehicle has dashed the motor cycle of the deceased from its back side.

It has not been brought on his cross-examination by the Insurance Company that the deceased was negligent in driving his motorcycle at the time of accident or he was also contributory negligence in the accident.

Two different stands have been taken by the Insurance Company in the cross-examination of the eye-witness that the deceased has stopped his motorcycle on the road all of sudden and subsequently they have taken the defence that the deceased has turned his motorcycle suddenly on his right side, therefore the accident occurred and thus, the Insurance Company itself was not sure in what manner the accident occurred but it is the eye-witness who have correctly deposed that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the vehicle who has dashed the motorcycle of the deceased from its back side.
Therefore, under the facts and evidence available on record, it cannot be said that the deceased was contributory negligent in accident.

10. So far as the next submission of the learned counsel for the appellant with effect to the acquittal of the non-applicant No.1 from criminal case is concerned, that would also not help the Insurance Company to avoid its liability because in a claim case, the strict rule of evidence is not applicable only preponderance of probability is to be seen which has been proved by the claimant by examining the oral as well as documentary evidence.
The non-applicant No.3 Insurance Company was having ample opportunity to prove their defence before the tribunal and to file relevant documents but they did not do so.
The acquittal of the non-applicant No.1 from the criminal case was of the year 2018 whereas the award of the claim case was passed in the year 2021.
In between that period the Insurance Company had not tried to led evidence with respect to the fact that the non-applicant No.1 was acquitted from the criminal case.
Even if the statement of another eye-witness is to be filed in the claim case, the same would not affect the merit of the claim case.

Until and unless it has been proved by the leading cogent and clinching evidence in support of the fact that the offending vehicle was not involved in the accident, it cannot be said that the award passed by the tribunal is unjustified or erroneous.

11. In the matter of Sunita & Others Vs Rajasthan State Road Transport Corporation & Anr.,
reported in AIR 2019 SC 994, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held in para 20 as under : -
"20.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is thus well settled that in motor accident claim cases, once the foundational fact, namely, the actual occurrence of the accident, has been established, then the Tribunal's role would be to calculate the quantum of just compensation if the accident had taken place by reason of negligence of the driver of a motor vehicle and,
while doing so, the Tribunal would not be strictly bound by the pleadings of the parties.

Notably, while deciding cases arising out of motor vehicle accidents, the standard of proof to be borne in mind must be of preponderance of probability and not the strict standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt which is followed in criminal cases.
12. At this stage, learned counsel for the appellant draws attention of this Court on the application filed by them under order 41 rule 27 of CPC.

By the said application the appellant seeks permission The Oriental Insurance Company Ltd vs Lallant Singh on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185750078/
4 to take additional evidence on record which are the true copy of the judgment dated 30.07.2018 passed by Chief Judicial Magistrate, Dantewada in Criminal Case No.65/2017, the copy of the deposition of Divesh Bear Naag PW-4, Shakahram PW-12.
13.

sentences.text: As it has been discussed earlier the judgment of criminal case is passed in the year 2018, whereas the impugned award of the present case is passed in the year 2021.

The Insurance Company was having ample opportunity to place these documents on record before the tribunal at the time of hearing of the case but they did not choose to do so and it is only when the award has been passed against them, they seeks permission to take additional evidence on record.

Even if the documents are being taken in record as an additional evidence it itself may not affects the merit of the case because the involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident has been found proved by the tribunal from the evidence of AW-4 Shakharam Kunjam and therefore, this Court is of the view that the additional evidence which is sought to be proved by the Insurance Company in this case is not relevant and vital which requires to be taken on record.
Hence, the application filed by the appellant Insurance Company under order 41 rule 27 of CPC is rejected.
14. From the foregoing discussions, this Court finds no merit in the appeal filed by the Insurance Company and is liable to be and hereby dismissed.
15. No order as to cost.
